name: Propylketobemidone
summary: Propylketobemidone is an opioid analgesic that is an analogue of ketobemidone. It was developed in the 1950s during research into analogues of pethidine and was assessed by the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime but was not included on the list of drugs under international control, probably because it was not used in medicine or widely available.

uses.text: The more commonly used ethyl ketone ("ethylketobemidone") is simply called ketobemidone, as it is the only drug of this family to have been marketed.

sideEffects.text: Presumably propylketobemidone produces similar effects to ketobemidone and other opioids, such as analgesia and sedation, along with side effects such as nausea, itching, vomiting and respiratory depression which may be harmful or fatal.

pharmacology.en: It is thought to act mainly as an agonist at the mu-opioid receptor, the same target as morphine. This relieves pain and causes euphoria and sedation, but also slows breathing.
pharmacology.zh: 一般認為它主要是 μ 鴉片受體的促效劑，作用目標和嗎啡相同。這會止痛並帶來欣快感和鎮靜，但也會抑制呼吸。
pharmacology.zhHans: 一般认为它主要是 μ 鸦片受体的促效剂，作用目标和吗啡相同。这会止痛并带来欣快感和镇静，但也会抑制呼吸。

fact.en: Its parent drug, ketobemidone, was first made in Germany in the 1940s and is still used as a painkiller in parts of Scandinavia.
fact.zh: 它的母體藥物 ketobemidone 於 1940 年代在德國首次合成，至今仍在北歐部分地區作為止痛藥使用。
fact.zhHans: 它的母体药物 ketobemidone 于 1940 年代在德国首次合成，至今仍在北欧部分地区作为止痛药使用。
